newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds pare gains following Fed tightening.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds pare gains following Fed tightening.

text.p: Canadian bonds weakened but continued to hold some of their earlier gains on Tuesday after the U.S. Federal Reserve hiked U.S. rates as had been widely predicted.
Analysts said Canadian bonds were taking their cue from softer U.S. Treasuries, which pared earlier gains to trade negative following the rate hike announcement.

"I don't sense any panic in the markets simply because a good portion of this has already been discounted. I would say people are just being a bit cautious," said Sheldon Dong, manager of fixed-income reseach with Midland Walwyn Capital.

Canada's 30-year benchmark was up C$0.15 to C$109.40 to yield 7.196 percent following the rate hike. Before the Fed announcement the bond had been trading up C$0.60 to C$109.85 to yield 7.159 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 12/32 to yield 6.95 percent following the rate hike. The spread between the two narrowed to 25 basis points from 29 basis points at the close of trading on Monday.
Analysts said the near term focus for Canadian bond investors has now shifted to the performance of the Canadian dollar.

As expected, the Bank of Canada did not immediately match the U.S. rate hike. The concern now is that the growing spread between Canadian and U.S. short-term administered rates could weaken the currency, analysts said.
"We're going to have to watch our currency a bit over the next few days," said Dong.
In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.0 percent bond due 2006 fell C$0.13 to C$102.77 to yield 6.604. The U.S. bond fell 11/32 to yield 6.75 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds widened to 15 basis points from 12 basis points on Monday.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 3.22 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.40 percent.
